title: Orthogonal component energy
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let a finite nonempty index set label a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one function. For a nonnegative integer $n$, a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and a coordinate subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the orthogonal component energy is the product-measure inner product of the orthogonal component of $f$ associated with $S$ with itself.

basis is algebraic and orthonormal for π
one basis vector is constant one
